steps.path: Automation details → a job waiting for you
steps.headline: Allow and Don't allow now take a note for the assistant; Don't allow needs one.
steps.changed: S-answer: the note tells the run what to do instead, so it doesn't just try again. Allow works with or without one.
steps.notice: Don't allow stays greyed out until the note has something in it.

steps.headline: An automation is linked to any number of pages and projects instead of belonging to one.
steps.changed: Q-pagejobs and Q-deletepage. Each link is its own box with Unlink; "Link to a page or project" adds one. Every linked page can run it from a button and shows its waiting dot.
steps.notice: The card's chips show every link (here Weekly briefing and youcoded-dev).

steps.headline: Missed runs gets more choices, and two new settings: Still running when due, and Runs on.
steps.changed: S-start: Missed runs adds "Run at another time" and "Run with other instructions" (which can also change what it makes). Q-overlap: skip the new run, stop the old one, or run both, per job. Q-devices: one switch per device.
steps.notice: With two devices on, a warning says it may run on each of them.

steps.headline: Run Claude jobs as ordinary Claude Code sessions that are saved, but kept in their own folder away from your chats?
steps.today: Claude jobs use Claude Code's background mode (the same Claude Code your chats use, started with no window). The last plan turned saving off, so a job waiting for you couldn't continue after a restart.
steps.problem: Not saving was only to keep runs out of your chat list. It cost the restart behaviour you asked about, and made Claude jobs work differently from ChatGPT / OpenRouter ones.
steps.proposal: Save each run like any Claude Code chat, but in a folder YouCoded keeps for automations and leaves out of your chat list, Resume and chat search. Old runs are deleted with the last-50 rule.

options.label: Saved, kept apart
pros: A waiting Claude job picks up exactly where it paused, even after a restart, like the other models.
Asks go through the same permission system your Claude chats already use.
cons: Run files sit on disk in that folder (deleted after 50 runs per job).

options.label: Not saved
cons: A Claude job waiting when you close YouCoded is lost, or has to start over.

steps.headline: Anthropic's rules allow an app to start your own, unchanged Claude Code with your own sign-in, which is what this does.
steps.changed: Their rules forbid apps that take your Claude login themselves, change Claude Code, or resell usage. YouCoded does none of those: you sign in inside Claude Code, and each run counts toward your plan's normal limits.
steps.notice: One grey area: their general terms discourage automated use, while their own docs offer scheduled Claude Code runs. Heavy automations on a subscription carry that small risk; jobs on ChatGPT or OpenRouter don't.

steps.headline: Both kinds of job follow the same permission list; only who enforces it differs.
steps.changed: Claude jobs: Claude Code enforces it, and anything set to Asks first reaches YouCoded the same way a Claude chat's permission question does. ChatGPT / OpenRouter jobs: YouCoded's own assistant enforces it.
steps.notice: S-allowed note: on both, a tool the job may never use is taken out of the assistant's list entirely, so it knows not to plan around it.

steps.path: Permissions → Other websites / Other commands and files
steps.headline: "Other websites" decides what happens when a job tries a website you didn't list. Is that clear now?
steps.changed: Example: the price watch lists bestbuy.com. If it tries amazon.com, "Never" refuses it (the run carries on and its box says what was refused); "Asks first" pauses it like any Asks first item. "Other commands and files" works the same for your computer.
steps.notice: New automation shows both as Never; you can change them while creating it or later.

steps.headline: "Approvals" decides what a run does when it reaches something set to Asks first. Is that clear now?
steps.changed: Example: the email sorter wants to send a reply. "Wait for me": the run pauses, you get a notification, and the job sits under Waiting for you until you answer or "Wait up to" runs out. "Skip and continue": the reply isn't sent, the run finishes, and its box says what was skipped.
steps.notice: It's what you saw on the details popup in round 2; nothing new to build.

steps.headline: Should New automation start with its settings already picked, or blank until you choose each one?
steps.today: You're right: every setting applies to every run the same way, from the first to the hundredth. "Default" only meant what New automation shows already picked.
steps.problem: Pre-picked is quicker but easy to skip past; blank makes you think about each one but is slower.

options.label: Already picked
options.summary: Wait for me, missed runs run once on wake, unlisted things Never, all three notifications on.
pros: The picks are the careful ones.
cons: You may not notice a setting you'd have changed.

options.label: Blank
options.summary: Create stays greyed out until each setting is chosen.
cons: Several more clicks for every new job, including ones made from a chat.

steps.headline: When notifications are sent, and what they show.
steps.changed: Needs you: the moment a run pauses for your OK. Has news: when a run ends and says it found something. Failed: when a run fails or reaches its limit. Each shows the job's name and one line; clicking opens that job. Where your system supports buttons in notifications, Allow and Don't allow appear right there.
steps.notice: Never for a run that finished with nothing to report.

steps.headline: Build only automation notifications now, and make the full Notifications menu its own follow-up?
steps.today: Settings has a Sound item for chat chimes. Automations would add the app's first system notifications.
steps.problem: Your S-notify note wants a full Notifications menu replacing Sound, covering chats finishing or waiting too. That's a bigger, separate job.
steps.proposal: Yes: step 4 ships the three switches per automation; the Notifications menu becomes its own work item, built next to this. No: the menu is part of step 4.

steps.headline: No limit on how many automations run at once.
steps.changed: Q-parallel: you picked no limit, since one job can be heavy and ten can be light.
steps.notice: If it ever slows the computer, a setting can be added later.

steps.headline: Build the Runs on list now and let the mesh sync work carry automations to your other devices?
steps.today: The mesh sync design (another session) plans "one list everywhere" for chats, then automatic choice of which device runs things, including "exactly-once" claims for scheduled automations.
steps.problem: Showing automations on every device needs that sync. Building a separate sync just for automations would be thrown away when the mesh lands.
steps.proposal: Each automation gets a stable identity and its Runs on list now (pictured); until the mesh's list step ships, only this device appears. When it ships, automations ride along, and later the mesh can pick the device itself.

options.label: Ride on the mesh
pros: Fits the mesh's later automatic device choice.
cons: Until then, your phone doesn't see automations made on the computer.

options.label: Sync now
cons: A temporary sync to replace later; risk of runs on both devices before the mesh's exactly-once claim exists.

steps.path: Deleting a page that has linked automations
steps.headline: Deleting a page asks about each linked automation: keep it or delete it.
steps.changed: Q-deletepage: the delete popup lists every automation linked to that page, each with Keep / Delete. A kept one loses that link but carries on as before, and still runs from Automations.
steps.notice: Not drawn yet; it will be on the deck after the build.

steps.prompt: Anything to add, question or change
steps.headline: Anything else before the build starts?
steps.today: This round covers every note from the last deck.
